📖 How To Read An Orderbook
The Raw Truth of a Market
The orderbook is every buyer, every seller, every price they're willing to trade at — in real time. Learn to read it, and you see exactly what algos, whales, and market makers are actually doing. Not what they're tweeting. What they're doing.
Anatomy of an Orderbook
PRICE The price level a buyer or seller has posted a resting order at.
SIZE How much they want to trade at that specific price. In perps: contracts or base currency.
TOTAL Cumulative size from top of book down — how much you'd fill if you swept every level from best price to here.
Six Signals in Every Book
📏 Spread
The gap between the best bid and the best ask. Tight (e.g. $0.10 on BTC) = deep liquidity, easy entries and exits. Wide spread = thin market — you'll slip on market orders. If it's wide, use LIMITS or wait for it to compress.
📊 Bid / Ask Depth
Total resting size on each side within a range (usually 1–2%). If bids >> asks near price, buyers are stacked supporting the level. If asks dominate, there's a ceiling. Depth is the market's skeleton.
🧱 Liquidity Walls
A single massive order 5–20 ticks off the top is a wall. Buy walls support price; sell walls cap it. But watch: walls often get pulled seconds before price hits them — they're bait to trick you into positioning wrong.
👻 Spoofing
Fake orders posted then cancelled to fake demand/supply. If a giant order appears then vanishes in seconds, it was a spoof. Real institutional flow doesn't flash — it either fills or sits patiently. Illegal on regulated venues, rampant in crypto.
🛡️ Absorption
Aggressive market orders slam a resting wall and price doesn't move — the wall is real and someone with size is absorbing the flow. This often marks a reversal point. Big money accumulating while retail panics.
🧊 Iceberg Orders
Only a small slice of the true order is visible; when it fills, another slice appears at the same price. Repeated fills at one level = iceberg. Signals a serious buyer/seller working large size without spooking the tape.
Before You Click Buy — The 5 Questions
  1. 1
    Is the spread reasonable? If wide → use a LIMIT, never market.
  2. 2
    Which side is heavier? Bias with the depth, not against.
  3. 3
    Any walls near your stop or target? They become magnets — or brick walls.
  4. 4
    Any spoofs pulled recently? Someone's trying to move you — step back.
  5. 5
    Is the last trade eating bids or lifting offers? That's the aggression direction — trade with it.
Common Book Patterns
Stack Layered orders at close prices creating a wall zone.
Sweep A market order that eats multiple price levels instantly.
Refill Depth restored immediately after being taken — a strong directional signal.
Vacuum Orders pulled just before price arrives — support / resistance was a lie.
Skew Persistent imbalance between bid and ask depth over time — regime bias.
